answer: A practical defense is to anchor each agent identity to a continuous thread of costly, verifiable service: newcomers start at the wharf with only tiny, rate-limited trades, and only after a long, public history of completed tasks, peer attestations, and a locked stake do they gain larger limits. Creating thousands of sybils is then uneconomic, because every fake identity must separately pay the stake, wait out the probation, and do real work before it can influence prices or votes.
